requirements.title: A, AT, and G character editing item rules
requirements.definition: A editing is used with a character effective item; AT is used with a character effective item in output only and shall not be used for input; G may edit character data; character kind is implied by the effective item.

pending.AT-input-invalid: Negative source shape: READ('xy','(AT)') c; repair to A editing. The sole changed property is using AT for input; no diagnostic phase or message is asserted.
pending.kind-implied-by-item: Source-control only for nondefault character kinds: the corresponding item kind selects the transfer kind, but kind availability and representation are processor dependent.

requirements.title: AT output trims trailing blanks and all-blank values produce no output
requirements.definition: AT field width is the length after trailing blanks are removed; output is that trimmed value, and all-blank values produce no output by the descriptor.

pending.AT-all-blank-produces-no-output: WRITE(buf,'(AT,"Z")') '   '; expect exactly 'Z' because AT transmits no characters and the following string descriptor writes at the current position.

requirements.title: Character output containing NEW_LINE characters may split stream records as slash editing
requirements.definition: For stream access, non-newline characters are written successively and each NEW_LINE character causes slash-like record termination and creation of a new current record.

pending.stream-nonnewline-successive: Internal WRITE cannot exercise stream-record splitting; source-control plan for a future external stream fixture must write characters before and after NEW_LINE and compare exact records without assuming behavior for internal files.
pending.stream-newline-slash-positioning-unasser: Unassertable in this source packet because the rule is specific to files connected for stream access, while this packet creates no file/I/O-unit fixtures.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_138.json. The reviewer re-derived the receipt (21 sections, 64 units, 0 hash mismatches) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-PARTITIONED the four crowded pages - p303, p304, p306 and p307 - unit by unit, confirming among other things that 13.8.8 genuinely owns only p1 despite covering six rounding-mode descriptors. A mis-attributed paragraph would have been invisible in the totals, since 64 would still be 64. The zero-numbered-R/C claim was verified: R1323 appears on p302 but belongs to the sibling 13.7.2.4 packet. FOUR blocking findings, all closed. C138SR-001: a negative was filed against 13.7.5.2.2, which only CROSS-REFERS to the rule - the actual prohibition is 13.7.5.1 p1 'On input, w shall not be zero' - and 'Note that w cannot be zero' is a reminder, not a prohibition; the facet is now an explicit dependency. C138SR-002: four units filed LATITUDE AS REQUIREMENTS - the fifth occurrence of the mixed obligation/latitude class, and notably the MIRROR of the sibling packet, which filed obligations as permission; all four were split into requirement and permission subunits. C138SR-003: an output-control facet sat under 13.9 p1, which owns only the input prohibition; output moved to p2. C138SR-004: a negative named a descriptor but NO DATUM, so nothing showed the p6 branch was reached; it now uses datum zero with (G4.1E3), where s=1 reaches the F branch, n=e+2=5 and w-n=-1, with repair (G7.1E3) expecting exactly '0.     ' - the reviewer derived all of that independently. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
